content.content:
put:
      description: |
        Creates a new dashboard with the given ID if none exists, or replaces the complete state of an
        existing one.

        > warn
        > This is a full replacement. Any panels not included in the request body are permanently
        > removed. To make targeted changes, retrieve the current state first with
        > GET /api/dashboards/{id}, apply your changes, and submit the full updated object.

        You can optionally include `access_control.access_mode` to change the dashboard access mode.
        If the authenticated user is not authorized to change access mode for the target dashboard,
        the request returns a `403` response with a descriptive `message`.
      operationId: put-dashboards-id
      parameters:
        - description: A required header to protect against CSRF attacks
          in: header
          name: kbn-xsrf
          required: true
          schema:
            example: 'true'
            type: string
        - description: The unique ID of the dashboard to be created or updated
          in: path
          name: id
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Kibana_HTTP_APIs_kbn-dashboard-data'
      responses:
        '200':
          content:
            application/json:
              examples:
                updateDashboardResponse:
                  description: |
                    The complete updated dashboard state after a full replacement. Note that `meta.created_at` is not returned in update responses - use the GET endpoint to retrieve it.
                  summary: Update dashboard response
                  value:
                    data:

                        auto_apply_filters: true
                        hide_panel_borders: false
                        hide_panel_titles: false
                        sync_colors: false
                        sync_cursor: true

                              - A line chart based on an ES|QL query

                               

                               

                              [Learn more about dashboards](https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/dashboards)

content.text: The PUT body takes the dashboard fields at top level. I'll save a backup of the current state, then add the new bar panel (count by `host.keyword`) below the existing two, and PUT the full object.

input.command:
S=/tmp/eff-82cf9avo/work/tmp/claude-0/-tmp-eff-82cf9avo-work/0da1e72d-e9d9-58d9-b388-fca8d0eba393/scratchpad && cat > $S/add_panel.py <<'EOF'
import copy, json, uuid, sys
src = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
data = copy.deepcopy(src["data"])
template = data["panels"][1]  # "Requests by response code" bar chart
panel = copy.deepcopy(template)
panel_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
panel["id"] = panel_id
panel["grid"] = {"x": 0, "y": 12, "w": 24, "h": 12}
cfg = panel["config"]
cfg["title"] = "Requests by host"
layer = cfg["layers"][0]
layer["x"]["fields"] = ["host.keyword"]
data["panels"].append(panel)
json.dump(data, open(sys.argv[2], "w"), indent=2)
print("added panel", panel_id)
EOF
python3 $S/add_panel.py $S/dash_get.json $S/dash_put.json && python3 -c "
import json; d=json.load(open('$S/dash_put.json'))
p=d['panels'][2]; print(p['grid'], p['config']['title'], p['config']['layers'][0]['type'], json.dumps(p['config']['layers'][0]['x']))" && curl -sS -X PUT -H "kbn-xsrf: true" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: ApiKey $KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY" "$KIBANA_URL/api/dashboards/study-seed-site-health" -d @$S/dash_put.json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('panels:', len(d['data']['panels'])); print([p['config']['title'] for p in d['data']['panels']])"
